bull.b: The company has expanded revenue substantially over several years, showing growing adoption of its molecular diagnostic portfolio. Recent year-over-year and sequential growth, together with reiterated 2026 guidance, supports a durable opportunity to increase testing volume and clinical reach.

Gross margins near or above 60% indicate attractive underlying economics for the testing business and provide a foundation for operating leverage. If revenue growth continues, these margins can support reinvestment in commercialization and help the company progress toward sustainable profitability.

Peer-reviewed clinical evidence and ongoing product-development initiatives can strengthen physician confidence in the portfolio and broaden its relevance across urology and pathology. This supports differentiation, adoption, and potential expansion beyond the company’s existing prostate cancer testing base.

bear.b: Higher debt combined with negative equity materially reduces financial flexibility and increases reliance on lenders or new capital. This structure can constrain investment in growth, raise refinancing and dilution risk, and make the business more vulnerable if operating improvement takes longer than expected.

The company is not yet self-funding despite improved cash-burn trends and revenue growth. Persistent operating losses and negative free cash flow require continued execution and external financing, limiting capital-allocation flexibility and increasing the risk that future funding will be needed before profitability is achieved.

The ExoDx acquisition is expanding the platform but currently weighs on earnings through higher operating expenses and an unfavorable product mix. Until integration produces sufficient revenue and cost synergies, margin pressure may delay the company’s path to positive EBITDA and sustainable earnings.
